text:
Sam: Quick follow-up to the RFC thread — we need a concise operator <-> control-plane guardrail sketch so infra can implement safely and ops can audit behavior.
Jess: Agreed. Do we want a declarative CRD that tenants create, or an imperative control-plane push API?
Sam: Prefer declarative. Tenants write a ScaleIntent CRD, operator reconciles to pool allocations and enforces guardrails.
Anita: Pushed a small CRD sketch to the doc repo. Minimal to start: code block below.
```
apiVersion: infra.redwood.io/v1alpha1
kind: ScaleIntent
metadata:
  namespace: team-foo
spec:
  qpsTarget: 120
  latencySLO: "p95<150ms"
  minGpus: 2
  maxGpus: 8
  burstWindow: 30m
  prewarm: true
status:
  allocatedGpus: 3
  state: "Allocated"
  operatorMessage: "within quota"
```
Mike: Two immediate gaps I see: 1) billing linkage — need a clear tag on any allocation for finance to reconcile reserved minutes. 2) Liveness: TTL or heartbeat so we don't hold prewarm forever if tenant abandons intent.
Jess: For guardrails: implement an admission webhook that enforces per-tenant caps and denies or mutates requests exceeding limits. If mutated, CRD status should record a human-readable reason and a fallback hint (e.g., route->hosted).
Sam: Operator needs the authority to mutate operator-managed fields but we should limit the surface. Proposal: only `status.operator*` fields are operator-writable; spec is tenant-owned but webhook can reject or mutate non-critical fields.
Anita: Also adding headroom/burst accounting: suggest fields `burstWindow` (duration) and `burstCredits` (int). Credits consumed for fast upscales; operator decrements and records consumption in status.
Mike: We rely on runtime metrics for signals: qps, tokens-per-request, kv_cache_hit_ratio, gpu_util. Need a documented ingestion schema. Where will kv_cache_hit_ratio come from? runtime exporter per pool.
Sam: Ops contract: operator expects OTLP metrics with labels: pool, tenant, model, kv_cache_hit, gpu_util, cpu_util. We'll publish spec in ops playbook.
autoscaler-bot: CI: scale-integration/pr-512 passed on staging 2145678922 :white_check_mark: p95=138ms, burst accounting verified.
Jess: Rollout plan: feature-flag gated; opt-in tenants via ScaleIntent; start with internal canary tenants; tighten admission policy over time; default fallback to hosted if throttled.
Anita: Add `evictionGraceSeconds` and `drainPolicy` enum (graceful|force) to make eviction explicit. Also note CRD versioning path v1alpha1 -> v1beta1 with migration steps.
Mike: Test plan: unit reconciliation tests, allocator shim integration tests, e2e failure injection (preempt, disk/image error), billing reconciliation tests, and burst load harness.
Sam: Ops checklist draft: 1) admission webhook + mutation rules 2) operator-managed status namespace 3) metrics ingestion schema 4) TTL + abandoned intent garbage collection 5) lease heartbeat with traceable logs 6) billing tag propagation 7) feature flag + canary plan.
Jess: Who owns webhook and billing hooks? infra owns webhook; finance/ops owns billing tag scheme. Need RFC follow-up to assign owners and SLAs.
Anita: I'll PR the CRD + a short admission webhook README tomorrow and include an example local CLI shim to simulate ScaleIntent for dev.
Mike: I'll add the load tests and billing reconciliation checks. Can autoscaler-bot surface stale-intent alerts?
autoscaler-bot: scheduled-job: stale-intent-check created, runs hourly.
Jess: Action items noted: Anita (CRD + README + CLI shim), Mike (load & billing tests), Sam (ops contract + owners), Jess (canary plan & security review).
Sam: Cool. We'll sync in architecture sync two weeks out to finalize. Any objections?
Mike: No objections.
Jess: LGTM.
Anita: LGTM.
